## Database

MongoDB via Mongoose. Requires Node.js >=20.19.0 (Mongoose 9). Set `MONGO_URI` in `.env` (defaults to a local instance on 27017). The connection is opened in `loaders/index.js`, before the app is created — see that file for why. `GET /healthz` reports live connectivity (`mongoose.connection.readyState`); graceful shutdown (SIGTERM/SIGINT) closes the connection before the process exits. Note: `mongodb-memory-server` is included so tests can run against a real in-memory MongoDB without a local install, whether or not you also picked the testing module.

### Transactions

`utils/transaction.js` wraps Mongoose's session boilerplate into one call: `await withTransaction(async (session) => { /* pass { session } to every query in here */ });` — see the comment at the top of that file for a full example. **Requires MongoDB to be running as a replica set** (even a single-node one) — a plain standalone MongoDB instance doesn't support transactions at all — Mongoose's default retryable-writes behavior means the error you'll actually see is usually `This MongoDB deployment does not support retryable writes` (older driver/server combinations instead throw `Transaction numbers are only allowed on a replica set member or mongos`); the same file explains how to run one locally with Docker. Not using multi-document transactions? Leave `utils/transaction.js` alone — it costs nothing sitting unused. Note: the default `test/setup.js` here starts a standalone `MongoMemoryServer`, which also doesn't support transactions — swap in `MongoMemoryReplSet` from the same package if you need to test transactional code.
